paper.title: Pure Exploration with Multiple Correct Answers

unmapped: General fixed-confidence identification: finite answer set I, set-valued correct-answer map i*(mu), possibly several correct answers
Known structure: means restricted to a known set M subset of O^K
delta-correct strategies; sample complexity E[tau_delta] as delta -> 0
settings.definition_quote: We work in a given one-parameter one-dimensional canonical exponential family ... We assume that there is a finite domain $\mathcal I$ of answers, and that the \emph{correct answer} for each bandit model is specified by a set-valued function $i^*: \mathcal M \to 2^{\mathcal I}$.

unmapped: General fixed-confidence identification with set-valued correct-answer map i*(mu)
settings.definition_quote: Any $\delta$-correct algorithm verifies ... for any multiple answer instance $\vmu$ with sub-Gaussian arm distributions.

symbols.D_mu: D(mu) = max_{i in i*(mu)} max_{w in simplex} inf_{lambda in alt(i)} sum_k w_k d(mu_k, lambda_k)

source.label: thm:lbd
source.quote: Any $\delta$-correct algorithm verifies \liminf_{\delta\to 0}\frac{\ex_\vmu[\tau_\delta]}{\log(1/\delta)} \geq T^*(\vmu) \df D(\vmu)^{-1} where D(\vmu) = \max_{i\in i^*(\vmu)} \max_{\w \in \triangle_K} \inf_{\vlambda \in \neg i} \sum_{k=1}^K w_k d(\mu_k,\lambda_k) for any multiple answer instance $\vmu$ with sub-Gaussian arm distributions.

results.notes: Algorithm class: all delta-correct algorithms. Bound on expected stopping time.

symbols.D_mu: D(mu) = max_i D(mu, alt(i)) characteristic divergence

conditions: i_F(mu) (set of oracle answers) is a singleton, e.g. single-answer problems

source.label: th:tas_sample_complexity
source.quote: For all $\vmu\in\mathcal{M}$ such that $i_F(\vmu)$ is a singleton (in particular all single-answer problems), Track-and-Stop with C-tracking is $\delta$-correct with asymptotically optimal sample complexity.

results.notes: Asymptotic optimality interpreted as lim E[tau]/log(1/delta) = 1/D(mu), matching Theorem 1. Extends GK16 to non-unique oracle weights.

symbols.D_conv: min over w in convex hull of oracle weights w*(mu) of D(w, mu)

source.label: th:tas_sample_complexity_general
source.quote: Let $\conv(A)$ be the convex hull of a set $A$. For all $\vmu\in\mathcal{M}$ in a multi-answer problem, Track-and-Stop with C-tracking is $\delta$-correct and verifies \lim_{\delta \to 0} \frac{\ex_\vmu[\tau_\delta]}{\log(1/\delta)} \leq \max_{\w\in \conv(\w^*(\vmu))} \frac{1}{D(\w, \vmu)}.

results.notes: Suboptimal in general for multiple-answer problems.

tuning: beta(t, delta) = log(C t^2/delta) with C >= e sum_t (e/K)^K (log^2(C t^2) log t)^K / t^2

source.quote: For $\beta(t, \delta) = \log(C t^2/\delta)$, with $C$ such that $C \geq e \sum_{t=1}^{+\infty} (\frac{e}{K})^K \frac{(\log^2(Ct^2)\log(t))^K}{t^2}$, Sticky Track-and-Stop is $\delta$-correct.

results.notes: delta-correctness: P(tau<inf and correct answer) >= 1-delta, so error probability <= delta. Follows from GK16 Prop. 12.

symbols.D_mu: D(mu) = max_i D(mu, alt(i)) characteristic divergence

tuning: f(t) = C t^10 for small confidence region

source.label: th:STaS_optimal_sample_complexity
source.quote: Sticky Track-and-Stop is asymptotically optimal, i.e. it verifies for all $\vmu\in\mathcal{M}$, \lim_{\delta \to 0} \frac{\ex_\vmu[\tau_\delta]}{\log(1/\delta)} \to \frac{1}{D(\vmu)}.

results.notes: Matches the lower bound of Theorem 1 for all mu in M.
